title: Design Style
intro: Use these rules to build Crimson editor tools with a consistent layout, typography, and interaction behavior. Measurements use logical pixels and scale with the Godot editor.

sections.title: Spacing
sections.description: Use a small spacing scale to show which controls belong together. Align labels and edges across the same pane.

items.label: xxs
items.description: Example use within compact labels or between related marks.

items.label: xs
items.description: Example use between closely related controls and small button content.

items.label: sm
items.description: Example inset between popup rows and the popup frame.

items.label: md
items.description: Example gap between peers, an icon and its label, or adjacent dialog actions.

items.label: lg
items.description: Example gap between small groups, cards, or toolbar regions.

items.label: xl
items.description: Example gutter around work panes and settings forms.

items.label: xxl
items.description: Example inset around confirmation panels and catalog sections.

items.label: Measured exceptions
items.description: Use the reference inset where a component needs it. The compact Select uses a 5 px anchor gap. Graph sockets use their native position and maintain space for labels.

sections.title: Typography
sections.description: Use the bundled Inter Variable for editor UI. Keep body and labels compact, and use weight and spacing for hierarchy.

items.label: Body and commands
items.description: Use for fields, menu commands, action rows, and graph port labels.

items.label: Secondary copy
items.description: Use for hints and section labels. Keep it visibly distinct from disabled content.

items.label: Workspace title
items.description: Use for the active panel title. Give the title enough room before the first row.

items.label: Content tabs
items.description: Use a thin underline the width of the active label and retain a quieter baseline across the tab strip.

sections.title: Colors
sections.description: Use surface and text roles consistently. Keep status and type colors local to the element they describe.

items.label: Canvas
items.description: The editor shell and canvas.

items.label: Sidebar
items.description: Recessed navigation and secondary regions.

items.label: Workspace
items.description: The main content or editing surface.

items.label: Search popup frame
items.description: The header and outside surface of a search popup.

items.label: Command menu
items.description: The surface shared by command menus and search results.

items.label: Main text
items.description: Labels and content that need normal emphasis.

items.label: Muted text
items.description: Metadata, hints, and inline descriptions.

items.label: Primary action
items.description: The most important action in the current group.

items.label: Destructive confirmation
items.description: The explicit action that removes authored data.

items.label: Controls
items.description: Use for fields, select triggers, and active rows.

items.label: Popup and dialog shell
items.description: Give the outer surface one subtle edge. Dialog corners reveal the dimmed owner content.

items.label: Pills and utility buttons
items.description: Use half the control height as the radius for compact primary actions, switches, and circular tools.

items.label: Graph pins
items.description: Use a dot for single values, a grid for arrays, paired columns for dictionaries, a list mark for enums, and a directional mark for execution. Fill a connected pin.

items.label: Hover
items.description: Use a small change in surface or text. Keep the control in place.

items.label: Active and selected
items.description: Distinguish an open control from a committed option. In a Select, keep the trailing check on the committed value as the highlight moves.

items.label: Keyboard
items.description: Keep native keyboard navigation and return focus on dismissal. Use the current row, active tab, or caret for orientation.

items.label: Read-only and disabled
items.description: Keep readable values and useful tooltips. Use a forbidden cursor for disabled interactions.

items.label: Tree and Inspector
items.description: Use a shared tree for hierarchy. Keep each binding on one row, and put settings for the selected row in the adjacent Inspector.

items.label: Menus and pickers
items.description: Group related commands. Add a separator between distinct groups. Use search for long or categorized choices.

items.label: Editor dialog
items.description: Put the prompt or form in the owning workbench, with the footer on the right. Cancel restores the previous context. Use a larger destructive action only when the operation removes authored data.

items.label: Graph
items.description: Keep nodes and pins on the canvas. Put properties, variables, and debug information in their task-specific panes.

items.label: Atoms
items.description: A button, field, checkbox, or another individual control covers one interaction or purpose.

items.label: Molecules
items.description: Combine atoms into a reusable pattern such as a labeled field, asset row, picker, or dialog footer.

items.label: Tool compositions
items.description: Bring reusable patterns together in a workbench. The Input Map owns actions and bindings. Visual Script owns graph authoring and debugging.

items.label: Button
items.description: A label or recognizable icon, a click target, and native command state. Give an icon-only button an accessible label.

items.label: Select
items.description: A trigger with the current value, an anchored popup, one row per option, and a trailing selection check.

items.label: Field
items.description: A concise caption, its input, and useful help. Show correction text near an invalid value.

items.label: Dialog
items.description: A scrim, rounded panel, title, optional form or explanation, and a footer with clearly labeled actions.

items.label: Graph node
items.description: A title, optional role or type accent, and typed rows with aligned pins. Compact variable getters use a single pill.
